headline: Monday's Rally Sets a Constructive Tone as Tuesday's Open Approaches
body_html:
Equity markets enter Tuesday's session carrying momentum from a broadly positive Monday close. Of the 544 names in our universe, 343 advanced against 198 declines, with Healthcare and Energy leading the way at gains of 1.82% and 1.79% respectively. Software added 1.57%, while Homebuilders bore the steepest pressure, shedding 2.02%, and Semiconductors slipped 0.72% — a pocket of weakness worth monitoring as the new session begins.

The headline move of Monday's session belonged to PTC Inc., which surged 33.49% after Schneider Electric announced a $22.6 billion agreement to acquire the industrial-software firm — a deal that also lifted Bentley Systems 7.82%. Freight brokerage RXO Inc. jumped 22.54%, while on the downside C.H. Robinson tumbled 10.85% and Lennar fell 6.73% as homebuilder sentiment remained fragile.

For Tuesday, traders will watch whether the Software sector can sustain its bid following the PTC catalyst, and whether Semiconductor names stabilize after Monday's drift. Homebuilders remain the sector to watch for continued rotation pressure. Pre-market tone and any early macro data releases will set the directional cue at the open.

briefs.headline: Schneider Electric's $22.6 Billion PTC Wager Reshapes Industrial Software
briefs.body: Schneider Electric's agreement to acquire PTC Inc. for $22.6 billion sent PTC shares soaring 33.49% on Monday, the largest single-session gain in our universe. The deal signals deepening corporate conviction that AI-enabled industrial software commands a significant premium, and peer names in the Software-Infrastructure space followed the stock higher.

briefs.headline: RXO Freight Surge Points to Renewed Logistics Optimism
briefs.body: RXO Inc. jumped 22.54% on Monday, standing as the session's second-biggest gainer. The freight brokerage's sharp move higher contrasts with the 10.85% decline posted by rival C.H. Robinson, suggesting investors are drawing sharp distinctions within the logistics sector rather than treating it as a monolith.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Face Continued Selling Pressure Ahead of Tuesday Open
briefs.body: The Homebuilders sector fell 2.02% on Monday, the worst performance across all tracked sectors. Lennar led decliners within the group, dropping 6.73%. With no immediate catalyst for relief visible in the pre-market, traders will be watching whether fresh economic data Tuesday provides any support for rate-sensitive housing names.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Tops the Sector Leaderboard on Biotech Strength
briefs.body: Healthcare's 1.82% advance on Monday was powered in part by Genmab, up 10.73%, and Azenta, which gained 10.27%. Biosimulation firm Certara added 7.59%. The cluster of gains across biotech and life-science tools names suggests broad conviction in the sector rather than a single stock-specific driver.

briefs.headline: Wall Street's AI Enthusiasm Broadens Beyond Megacap Names
briefs.body: Analyst commentary circulating Monday pointed to Microsoft's ongoing AI repositioning as a story with further room to run, with at least one longtime skeptic reversing course publicly. The shift in sentiment adds a fresh tailwind narrative heading into Tuesday's session, particularly for Software names that have lagged the AI trade.

briefs.headline: BPCL Targets $3 Billion Bond Market to Back Brazil Offshore Expansion
briefs.body: Indian state energy company BPCL is planning a $3 billion bond issuance to finance an offshore oil project in Brazil, underscoring how emerging-market energy firms continue to pursue large-scale capital raises in international debt markets. The move adds a global dimension to what has otherwise been a domestically driven Energy sector rally.
